svg.aria-label: How to write ಥ: 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 7 movements
svg.title: Writing ಥ
svg.desc: 7 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of ಥ (kannada), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansKannada-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-thha.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಥ, 43 frames, 4.3 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016) <https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Kannada-alphabet-thha.gif>. Source note on variation: The CC BY-SA 4.0 animation is filed under the slug "thha" and draws dental ಥ (U+0CA5); in this series "tha" animates dental ತ and "tta" retroflex ಠ, so the glyph was checked frame by frame rather than taken from the file name. It writes ಥ in four pen-down runs: from the upper left the pen goes down around the left lobe, up into the middle point, down around the right lobe, up the right side and back left across the top (frames 0–16); after a lift, the top bar from left to right curling up into the hook (frames 19–26); after a second lift, the tail below the point, drawn downward (frames 28–29); after a third lift, the dot in the middle (frame 31). The frames were read from a mirror copy that matches the Commons file's listed size (215×174, 123 KB), byte size and frame count. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Kannada outline rather than copying the animation's handwritten proportions; in that outline the bowl's top is fused into the bar, as in ದ, so the closing movement runs along the lower part of the bar's ink and the bar retraces it, and the dot is a filled disc, drawn as a small closed loop inside it. The three-lift order remains the same.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 strokes · 3 pen lifts · 7 movements
Stroke order after Gopala Krishna A, Kannada-alphabet-thha.gif, animation of Kannada consonant ಥ, 43 frames, 4.3 seconds (Wikimedia Commons, 25 May 2016)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
